dedupe_keys.name: lead tool low income energy affordability data 2022 update

description: The Low-Income Energy Affordability Data (LEAD) Tool was created by the Better Buildings Clean Energy for Low Income Communities Accelerator to help state and local partners understand housing and energy characteristics of the low- and moderate-income communities they serve. It estimates household energy data by income, energy expenditure, fuel type, housing type and geography, and its website lets users build and download heat maps and charts of housing, energy, demographic and education characteristics. The 2022 update draws mainly on the 2022 American Community Survey five-year Public Use Microdata Samples calibrated to 2022 EIA electric (Form 861) and gas (Form 176) utility data, and provides 60 files, 7.3 GB in all, for the 50 states, Puerto Rico and Washington, D.C., with their cities, counties, census tracts and tribal areas, plus a data dictionary and methodology. Coverage: the United States. Access: free OEDI download and web tool. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: values are modelled estimates, not billing records. Simulation uses are energy burden and housing characteristics by area for equity-focused retrofit and resilience planning. Related records: the EU Energy Poverty Advisory Hub indicators.
